evidenceStatus: Source and schema inspection only. No tests or HV executed in this slice.
applicationBoundary: Operator approval, fresh collision/drift checks, supported MCP writes/readback and later mock/real/HV gates required. This JSON is NOT executed.
preservedFields: All fields except title, body/condition, status and acceptanceCriteria for ten existing records; historical before images preserved. Two new records are proposals only.
historicalEvidencePolicy: Retain every original record and historical claim; no retirement or false recovered-AC provenance.

after.title: D64, tape and IEC media behavior matches immutable native VICE

acceptanceCriteria.text: For the same pinned D64 fixtures and operation sequence, sector reads/writes, returned semantic status, error-map effects and persisted bytes match native VICE; cover valid sectors, geometry boundaries, malformed/truncated input, read-only input, read errors and failed writes without treating success-only BAM reads as complete coverage.

True-drive IEC line contributions, both ATN edges, enabled/disabled drive cases, contention, drive motor/rotation progression and DOS-mediated BAM-read bytes/status/effects satisfy the separately proposed FR-ARCH-TRUEDRIVE-1541-002 criteria against the same native initial conditions. Direct image access cannot satisfy true-drive acceptance.

Datasette motor startup, delayed stop/cancellation, pulse delivery, sense-line wiring and recording on writable media satisfy the separately proposed FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 criteria for C64 and VIC-20. A metadata pulse read or in-memory recording count alone is insufficient.

Each accepted media scenario retains fixture/firmware/resource hashes, mode, initial state, clock domain, operation sequence, ordered observations and first mismatch. Reusing a host-cycle deadline as a drive/tape clock assertion or comparing different media modes is rejected.

All preceding assertions first pass with independent discriminating mocks and expected negative controls, then the same inputs/assertions pass with real providers and the full applicable suites. Missing, skipped, failing or mock-only evidence leaves the criterion unsatisfied.

after.body: Managed media behavior shall reproduce the pinned native VICE reference at the corresponding layer: D64 image-sector data/status/persistence, true-drive IEC and motor behavior, and machine-specific datasette timing/sense/record behavior. Image-buffer success, synthetic motor counters and historical test totals cannot substitute for real-emulator parity. Preserve the separate buffered and true-drive modes and all legacy evidence.

before.title: Media devices (D64, tape) I/O functional parity
before.body: D64DiskImageDevice sector R/W, motor ramp, BAM read all implemented. Datasette motor ramp, sense line, and record mode complete. Closes IEC ATN timing gap for Phase 1.

after.title: VIC-II RC, DMA and screen-memory checkpoints match immutable VICE

acceptanceCriteria.text: On PAL MOS6569, compare RC, VC, VCBASE, VMLI, idle and bad-line state immediately before and after the native VC/RC update events and across bad-line/idle transitions, including RC=7 with bad_line both false and true and timed DEN/YSCROLL changes.

After identical stable PAL initial conditions, both native and managed raster position return to the same position after 19656 full cycles and each cycle counter advances by exactly that amount. Check last-cycle/last-line wrap and samples at frame-minus-one, frame and frame-plus-one. Explicitly document the counter width and phase normalization.

For MOS6567R8, MOS8562, MOS6567R56A, MOS6572 and PAL MOS8565, compare the same sprite-3 DMA-active and bus-ownership observables at aligned model-specific cycle/phase boundaries. Include disabled/enabled sprite, Y match, next-line continuation, stop/release and bad-line overlap; a loose native line window plus an independent managed boolean does not pass.

With CPU and other memory writers controlled and identified, immediate screen-memory roundtrip and a PAL-frame c-access scenario compare both providers' full $0720-$07E7 fixture, relevant internal fetch effects and read/write direction. No emulation cycles may elapse during immediate roundtrip; matrix fetches must not issue screen-RAM writes, including writes of the existing value.

Keep all wider TR-CYCLE-001 criteria and visible-frame/lockstep gates mandatory. These checkpoint assertions must be proven with discriminating mocks first and identical real bindings later; historical nine/eleven-case claims, native-only checks, skips and mock-only runs cannot close this FR.

after.body: Managed VIC-II shall match the pinned VICE x64sc model at equivalent initial conditions and explicitly aligned cycle/phase checkpoints for RC/VC state, raster progression, sprite DMA, bus ownership and screen-memory access. Include the legacy five named variants without calling MOS8565 non-PAL. These checkpoints support visible-frame parity but do not alone establish full pixel/audio/workload lockstep, which remains mandatory under the wider plan and TR-CYCLE-001.

before.title: VIC-II visible-frame parity (RC window, DMA checkpoints, screen-RAM)
before.body: VIC-II RC/VC state machine matches VICE cycle-accurate behavior (RC window). Native checkpoints validate sprite DMA for all 5 non-PAL models. Screen RAM survives one PAL frame unchanged. VICE viciisc/vicii-cycle.c:541-563, vicii-fetch.c:135-166.

after.title: Paired PAL screen-memory frame checkpoint

acceptanceCriteria.text: Seed both providers with all 200 address-distinct bytes, record initial register/bank/raster/phase state, and compare every byte before and after exactly 19656 full PAL cycles with CPU and unrelated writers controlled. Native and managed use the same fixture and phase boundary.

Retain c-access activity evidence and actor/direction information sufficient to distinguish VIC reads/internal buffer updates from external RAM writes; detect a same-value write that a final-byte comparison would miss.

Reject wrong start/end address, one omitted byte, one changed byte, one-cycle drift, absent c-access activity, wrong bank and a fixture corrupted identically on both sides. Compare to independently pinned expectations, not just mutual equality.

after.body: The managed and pinned native PAL VIC-II shall perform equivalent controlled screen-memory frame scenarios. The 200-byte legacy fixture starts at $0400 + 20*40 = $0720 and ends at $07E7. Attribute memory effects by actor; no pixel-parity claim follows from a RAM-only checkpoint.

before.title: VIC-II native screen-RAM visible-frame checkpoint
before.body: Native VICE screen RAM (-) survives one full PAL frame (19,656 cycles) unchanged. VIC-II c-access DMA is read-only. VICE vicii-fetch.c:135-166.

after.title: PAL raster and cycle-count frame periodicity

acceptanceCriteria.text: From a recorded nonzero raster position and separately from the last cycle of the last line, both providers match the pinned raster sequence at frame-minus-one, frame and frame-plus-one; only the exact 19656-cycle sample repeats the starting phase/position.
Each provider's counter delta is exactly 19656 full cycles for the frame interval, with explicit modular arithmetic if a counter wraps and no double-counting of half-cycle observations.
Expected negative controls reject 62/64-cycle PAL lines, 311/313-line frames, off-by-one samples, phase swaps and a counter that freezes while raster wraps correctly.

after.body: PAL MOS6569 raster progression shall match pinned native VICE with 63 full cycles per line and 312 lines per frame. Preserve exact cycle-count and raster-position checks while making initialization, phase and wrap semantics explicit.

before.title: VIC-II PAL raster position frame-periodic
before.body: Managed PAL VIC-II raster (rasterLine, rasterX) returns to identical position after exactly one frame (312x63=19,656 cycles). VICE vicii-cycle.c:576-598.

after.title: VICE-ordered RC, VC, VCBASE, VMLI and idle transitions

acceptanceCriteria.text: Before/after the PAL VC update event, assert VC, VCBASE, VMLI and RC for bad-line and non-bad-line states, using nonzero VC/VMLI fixtures that detect a missing reset or swapped assignment.

At the RC event, exhaust RC 0..7 crossed with idle true/false and bad_line true/false at the contract seam. Assert the entire resulting tuple, including RC=7/bad_line=true yielding captured VCBASE, wrapped RC=0 and idle=false. Classify naturally reachable real traces separately from seam-only transition fixtures.

Run reachable PAL multi-line traces covering bad-line entry, seven row advances, idle entry and exit, and timed DEN/YSCROLL changes. Pin allow-bad-lines and line-range prerequisites so YSCROLL equality alone is never assumed sufficient.
Sample immediately before/after both update events and on neighboring cycles. Document cycle numbering and tick entry/exit alignment; reject a correct value reported one phase/cycle late.

Negative controls independently corrupt each tuple member or operation order and are rejected inside a passing mock suite. The same assertion logic is used for real native/managed observations; absent native observability remains an unsatisfied gate, not inferred parity.

after.body: Match vicii-cycle.c:541-563 and the selected model cycle flags. At the VC event, assign VC=VCBASE and VMLI=0, and RC=0 on a bad line. At the RC event, RC=7 first sets idle and captures VCBASE=VC; then non-idle or bad-line state increments RC modulo eight and clears idle. Preserve the native operation order and explicitly align managed observation timing.

before.title: VIC-II RC window state machine cycle-accurate
before.body: VIC-II row counter (RC) and video counter (VC) state machine matches VICE viciisc/vicii-cycle.c:541-563. VC update at RasterX=13: vc=vcBase, vmli=0, bad line sets rc=0. RC update at RasterX=57: rc==7 sets idle; if not idle or bad line, rc=(rc+1)&7.

after.title: Model-specific sprite DMA and ownership checkpoints

acceptanceCriteria.text: Resolve each native selector and managed model to the same pinned model identity, timing geometry and resources. Reject a fallback model, wrong PAL/NTSC classification or timing-table mismatch.

For sprite 3/Y=$50, retain a full aligned trace from before activation through next-line continuation and release, plus disabled-sprite and Y-nonmatch controls. Compare the same DMA-active bit and ownership fields independently, not merely any event near lines $4F-$51.

Exercise no-bad-line and bad-line-overlap fixtures with explicit DEN, YSCROLL, allow-bad-lines and relevant register-write timing. Validate combined ownership and release against native rather than attributing every stolen cycle to sprite DMA.

Mock controls reject right line/wrong cycle, right cycle/wrong phase, wrong sprite, missing release, native-only event and substituted DMA-active-for-ownership signals. Real-binding receipts retain the formerly unused native cycle and first divergent field.

after.body: Retain all five legacy model cases: MOS6567R8 65x263, MOS8562 65x263, MOS6567R56A 64x262, MOS6572 65x312 and PAL MOS8565 63x312. Compare DMA-active, BA/AEC or equivalent documented CPU-ownership observations separately at corresponding cycle/phase boundaries. Do not equate sprite DMA-active with CPU-cycle stolen.

before.title: VIC-II non-PAL sprite DMA window native checkpoint
before.body: All 5 non-PAL VIC-II models (Mos6567, Mos8562, Mos6567R56A, Mos6572, Mos8565) fire sprite-3 DMA near line 0x50. Managed IsCpuCycleStolen true at (SpriteY+1, rasterX 0). VICE vicii-chip-model.c:272-403/437-566.

after.title: Matrix c-access has no external screen-RAM write effect

acceptanceCriteria.text: With pinned bank/address, bad-line and prefetch state, compare fetched byte/color and internal buffer index/effects against native at a defined checkpoint, including prefetched/delayed cases specified by the native source.

Capture attributable external-memory access direction so every matrix c-access is read-only with respect to screen RAM; include a negative control that writes the same value and would evade an unchanged-final-RAM check.

Separately identify allowed CPU/other-device writes. Reject a fixture with uncontrolled writers or absent c-access execution as insufficient evidence; do not infer VIC write behavior solely from frame-end bytes.

after.body: Model VICE vicii-fetch.c:76-100,192-201 as reads from selected memory and updates to VIC internal buffers. Do not confuse internal buffer writes with writes to external screen RAM, and do not claim other emulated actors are write-free.

before.title: VIC-II c-access DMA read-only semantics
before.body: VIC-II matrix DMA c-access reads screen RAM without write side-effects. Screen RAM bytes written before a frame remain unchanged after. VICE vicii-fetch.c:135-166.

after.title: Immediate screen-memory roundtrip with zero elapsed emulation time

acceptanceCriteria.text: For all 200 addresses, the address-distinct fixture roundtrips exactly in both providers and matches independent expected bytes; boundary sentinels immediately outside the fixture remain unchanged.
Record cycle/phase and raster state before and after the immediate operation sequence; assert no elapsed emulation time and no hidden step call.

Mock controls reject wrong address, truncated read, wrong byte, aliased neighboring addresses and a one-cycle hidden advance even when all returned bytes match. Preserve the same checks in real bindings.

after.body: Native and managed test adapters shall write and read the complete legacy screen-memory fixture at $0720-$07E7 without advancing emulated time. A successful adapter roundtrip proves address/data access only, not visible-frame or DMA parity.

before.title: VIC-II screen RAM immediate read-back
before.body: ViceNativeBridge ReadMemory/WriteMemory roundtrip for - returns written value in zero elapsed cycles. VICE c-access is read-only.

after.title: Paired VIC-II checkpoint contract, mock and real-provider gates

acceptanceCriteria.text: A scenario ledger maps every linked TR and FR checkpoint AC to concrete case IDs, inputs, expected observables, source pins, mock positive controls, single-fault negative controls and later real bindings; no AC is represented only by a count or test name.

The unfiltered native-safe mock suite passes with zero failed/skipped/unexecuted cases and rejects every planned wrong response as an expected assertion failure inside a passing test, including unchanged-value writes and wrong-phase ownership.

The same cases, inputs, expected values, assertions and interaction checks run against real native and managed providers, with native state/data tied to the pinned immutable build and an explicit model/phase adapter. Missing read-only observability blocks acceptance; native source patches are forbidden.

Full applicable cumulative and real-emulator gates run with retained stdout/stderr, TRX/diagnostics, exact command/filter/configuration, counts and first divergence. Native-unavailable skips, a loose line-window match or native-only RAM tests are not passing parity.

Independent hostile review must evaluate assertions, source pins, phase alignment, requirements and the whole plan; acceptance requires AGREE, accuracy/completeness each at least 98 and zero FAIL/UNKNOWN, with complete durable request/response and MCP verdict readback.

after.condition: Cover every criterion of TR-VIC-EDGE-001,002,004,005,006 using independently expected state/data plus paired native/managed observations. Retain the original four frame/memory cases and five sprite-model cases as provenance, not a fixed completion denominator. Add assertion-level boundary and wrong-response coverage before implementation.

after.title: Full RC/VC transition assertions and native-aligned traces

acceptanceCriteria.text: Enumerate every TR-VIC-EDGE-003 AC in a case ledger, including the RC/idle/bad-line cross product, nonzero VC/VCBASE/VMLI, adjacent event samples and reachable DEN/YSCROLL transitions. Tag seam-only states explicitly rather than inventing native reachable traces.

Prove each asserted tuple member, event timing and branch order discriminates correct and single-fault mock results, with all controls accepted/rejected as expected inside a fully green unfiltered native-safe suite.

Bind the same contract to production transition behavior and the reachable trace cases to aligned native/managed providers; record any unavailable field as a blocking observability gap. Real output must not become its own expected fixture.

Preserve full-suite and real trace receipts and independent AGREE with both scores at least 98 and zero FAIL/UNKNOWN before acceptance. Eleven source-declared cases or only RC/idle success cannot close untested VC/VCBASE/VMLI behavior.

after.title: D64 image-layer sector, status and persistence parity

acceptanceCriteria.text: For every valid sector of the standard 35-track 683-sector D64 fixture, compare all 256 bytes to independent address-derived expected bytes and native results. Exercise first/last sector in each zone, BAM 18/0 and legal/illegal neighboring track/sector boundaries. Inventory additional currently required D64 variants before fixing the full test denominator.

On disposable copies, write address-distinct patterns and compare immediate readback, fresh-open persisted bytes and whole-image differences to native. Only reference-observed data/error-map changes are accepted; validate error-map clearing on successful write and preserve native behavior when metadata persistence reports an error.

Cover read-only writes, out-of-range access, truncated input, injected read/write failures and error-map values, including hard errors that retain the caller buffer and soft errors that still transfer data. Compare semantic status plus actual buffer/image effects; do not assume every error implies atomic rollback.

The adapter records operation order, fixture hash, geometry, status mapping, bytes and flush/reopen outcomes without masking native distinctions. Wrong-byte, wrong-sector, false-success, lost-persistence and wrong-error-buffer controls must be rejected before real implementation begins.

after.body: At the image-sector layer, managed D64 behavior shall match pinned VICE disk_image_read_sector/disk_image_write_sector and fsimage_dxx read/write semantics through an explicit semantic adapter. Keep this separate from DOS/IEC true-drive execution. Define supported geometry and fixture variants from the current D64 product requirements before tests; do not silently add or remove image formats.

after.title: D64 sector I/O discriminating contracts and native parity

acceptanceCriteria.text: Map each D64 AC to data-driven valid/boundary/error cases, including all 683 standard-image sectors and every required image/error-map variant discovered in the approved geometry inventory. Give every case a fixed expected byte/status/effect tuple and source provenance before implementation.

Correct mocks pass every assertion; independently corrupted status, byte, sector offset, retained error buffer, error map, flush or fresh-open result is rejected by the corresponding assertion inside a green suite. No production code changes until this unfiltered mock gate is green.

Run the same cases/assertions through native and managed adapters on verified disposable inputs. Retain full-image before/after comparisons and fresh-open results, distinguish image-layer evidence from true-drive IEC evidence, and leave any unrepresented native error effect unsatisfied.

Retain chronological mock, implementation, real-provider and cumulative-suite evidence; require independent AGREE with accuracy/completeness at least 98 and zero FAIL/UNKNOWN before closing coverage. No suite is executed or claimed passing by this proposal.

after.condition: Add a dedicated D64 image-I/O contract suite for TR-MEDIA-D64-001 and FR-BACKFILL-MEDIA-001. Expected bytes and status/effect tuples derive from pinned native behavior and independently generated fixtures, not the managed implementation. Use temporary disposable copies for all writes, retaining original evidence fixtures.
